title: Single-Cell RNA-seq Reveals Immune Remodelling in Cervical Carcinoma
text:
This project investigates immune remodelling in cervical carcinoma using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis.
The workflow includes preprocessing of single-cell transcriptomic data, quality control, normalization, clustering, cell type annotation, differential expression analysis, and immune microenvironment characterization.

title: Dr. Sumaya Khan Mifty
text:
Dr. Sumaya Khan Mifty, MBBS is a physician and researcher at the intersection of genomics, bioinformatics and precision medicine.
Her work explores how genetic and clinical data can be translated into better understanding of disease and more individualized healthcare, with a particular interest in cardiovascular genetics and precision cardiology. She has research experience spanning clinical epidemiology, biomedical data science, and multidisciplinary collaborative research.
Beyond her own research, she is passionate about building research capacity and mentoring early-career researchers. Her long-term vision is to bridge clinical medicine with computational and genomic science to advance data-driven, patient-centered medicine.

From lecture halls to operating theatres, and now to code, data, and research.
I am Dr. Sumaya Khan Mifty, an intern doctor at Dhaka Medical College & Hospital with an interest in integrating clinical medicine with genomic research.
Alongside clinical practice, I am involved in research areas including environmental health, cardiovascular disease, epidemiology, and evidence synthesis. My work includes peer-reviewed publications, systematic reviews, international conference presentations, and collaborative research projects.
I am expanding my skills in R programming, GitHub, and reproducible research to support future work in genomic medicine, bioinformatics, and cardiovascular genetics. I am interested in applying computational approaches to improve disease understanding and precision medicine.

title: Heart Failure Guideline Adherence Study
text:
Heart failure remains a major cardiovascular health challenge, with significant morbidity, mortality, and healthcare burden. Despite advances in evidence-based therapies, gaps remain between guideline recommendations and routine clinical practice.
This ongoing study evaluates adherence to ESC guideline-directed heart failure management among hospitalised patients in tertiary care settings in Bangladesh.
